finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied 'f' parameter is joined to the root with filepath.Join, which cleans '..' segments but doesn't confine the result to the root. An unauthenticated attacker can read any file the process can access.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", which escapes root
file contents returned to the caller
handler registered on /dl with no auth middleware

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Join, no filepath.Base, no rejection of '..', no os.Root or fs.FS confinement, no authentication or authorization on the handler. Symlinks inside root are also followed. The /avatar handler is safe because it uses filepath.Base (files.go:22).

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param 'f' straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no prefix check, Base, or '..' rejection, and files.go:18 writes the contents back. files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth, so an anonymous caller can read files outside /srv/files with '../' sequences.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw 'f' query value to filepath.Join(root, name) and then os.ReadFile, with no Base, prefix check or auth, and files.go:18 returns the contents, so "../../etc/passwd" escapes /srv/files (files.go:32 registers /dl with no middleware).
